purpose: Local LV cable sizing that reproduces the supplied Cable Sizing workbook, with load-list suggestions, a load-list dashboard (filters, issues, bulk edit), a hand-calculation panel with size ladder, undo/redo, print/PDF reports, native workbook export and adjustable drum planning, and a schematic import that turns single-line diagrams, DB schematics and circuit schedules (PDF, DXF, images) into a reviewed load list.

scopeDecision.instructionBoundary: User requests take precedence over attached documents. The current workbook-based scope was explicitly confirmed after the archive was discovered. Do not silently restore the archived workflow.

quickStart.deploy: Static dist on a dedicated HTTPS origin. Vercel, Cloudflare Pages and Netlify header configuration is present. Production deployment has not been verified.

invariants: Keep all 41 Cable Sizing columns, their headings, input/list/calculated roles and dropdown narrowing unchanged.
sheet.ts reproduces the workbook, including blank diversity=1, THD=0, factors=1, parallel cables=1 and blank total VD when From is blank.
From/To links use the first matching To, as the workbook does. Do not silently change this rule; duplicate destinations should be avoided by engineers.
Electrical suggestions only fill blank inputs. Typed inputs are never overwritten. Cable run length is never suggested.
Built-in electrical ratings come from the supplied workbook, not an independent manufacturer PDF verification. IEC is not an active electrical source in this version.
Never hand-edit sizing-tables.json or resave the template with ExcelJS. Regenerate both from the original workbook via extract-workbook.mjs.
Export uses JSZip and sheet XML to preserve OFFSET-based dropdowns, formulas, formatting and lookup sheets. Excel recalculates on open.
All drum runs remain whole. Overlong runs are unplaced. First-fit decreasing is a heuristic, not proof of a minimum drum count.
A supplier capacity is valid only for its specified cable OD. Bending, payload and site lifting limits still apply.
Selecting a different load-list cable requires its physical dimensions and source to be confirmed before a drum count appears.

Keystone bend guidance is an optional reference for selected constructions, with editable multipliers and a source note; installation and fixed bend values never automatically set the drum barrel radius limit. Drum compatibility is an estimate against the entered limit, not supplier approval. Changing the linked cable clears guidance.
Imports, OCR, autosave and exports run in the browser. Runtime assets come from the site origin. The development server binds only to 127.0.0.1.
Update this semantic knowledge source when behaviour changes. Generated fingerprints do not automatically explain new business rules.
explain.ts, issues.ts and the dashboard derive every electrical value from sheet.ts results or evaluateRow; never add independent electrical maths to them.
Connected-load KPIs sum only final circuits (rows nothing is fed from) so board feeders are not double counted.
Undo/redo history lives in memory only; autosave and backups store the current project, not its history.
Screen colours use the app.css tokens only; text tokens keep at least 4.5:1 contrast in both themes.

Schematic import reads values only from drawing text. Anything worked out (system voltage from the board, phase from cores or voltage, kW from HP or kVA×PF, a feeder load summed from its circuits, copper assumed when the conductor is not stated) is listed in Candidate.inferred with its reason and shown in italics in the review. Cable run length is never inferred.

The load-list assistant never changes the sheet by itself: proposed changes need a tick and Apply, only real rows and input columns are accepted, and cable runs (AH) are never proposed. Panel import never guesses a panel: rows with no title or panel-named sheet stay without From and are flagged. A load list's "Load factor" column is never read as diversity (H). Export splits into one Cable Sizing sheet per panel only when no row feeds another listed panel, so Excel's total-VD chain is never cut.

AI reading talks only to http://127.0.0.1 or localhost on ports 11434 (Ollama) and 1234 (LM Studio); isLocalUrl and the CSP connect-src enforce it. Redirects and credentials are disabled. Before any prompt, Ollama must report cloud.disabled true or an LM Studio user must confirm on-device inference with LM Link off. An AI value is kept only when its quote is in the drawing text and the value is in the quote; kept values are Candidate.inferred and reviewed like any other. No hosted AI, API key or proxy.
Rows created from a "fed from" note alone start unticked: without a cable run they would blank total VD for every circuit below them.
Voltages, cores, sizes or cable types outside the workbook lists are kept as read and show as invalid on the sheet; the import never maps them to the nearest listed value.
Every saved sheet cell holds at most 300 characters (MAX_CELL); imports, pastes and inputs clip to it so autosave and backups keep working.
Numeric inputs follow Excel: only plain decimal numbers are numbers (0x1A, 0b11, Infinity are invalid). Exports never write non-finite cached values or XML-forbidden characters.

Untrusted files are size-checked before parsing: CSV/TSV ≤10,000 rows and ≤200 columns, images by header dimensions, PDF page/text/image limits, DXF line/text limits. Avoid spreading large arrays into function calls (Math.max(...), push(...)).

The app ships with no example project: the reference workbook is the source of the formulas and tables only. A fresh workspace is "Untitled project" with empty sheets and no cable runs; drum and cable specifications keep their editable defaults.
Drawing images are processed on the device only; image size is checked from the file header before decoding, OCR words are capped at 8,000 per pass and tracing is bounded (strokes, busbars, feeders).
Workbook columns A-AO keep their letters. Columns added to the workbook go after AO, with helpers after them; the export rewrites the filter range for any last column.

Load list to Cable sizing is one way: sending updates matching rows and appends new ones but never deletes, and editing Cable sizing never changes the Load list. Two items with the same From/To stay two rows. A value typed on a load-list row always wins over the catalogue, and a datasheet value reaches the catalogue only after the user ticks it.

Numeric comparisons follow 15 significant digits. RowResult.helpers exposes the step05 helper columns (keys AT–AY, workbook BY–CD since step09) and helpers.fault (earthing system, nominal U0, transformer Z, Ze, Ia, IΔn, CPC type/k/multiplier/size/resistance, Ik, times, energies, final circuit). Earth fault loop for TN-S and TT with RCDs and CPC (AP–BG) and short circuit (BH–BO) via faultCells, chained from the feeding row (Ze ← Zs BB, TT only from a TT row; fault level ← BM); CHECK_COLS/failsCheck list every PASS/FAIL column (AG, AN, BE, BG, BJ, BO, BT). Motor starting VD (step09 BP–BT): BR = AL + (multiple − 1) × AK with the multiple typed (BQ) or the starter type's value on Lists (TABLES.starters), checked against BS or Settings Def_StartVD (15 %).

Each build verifies the approved release file list, the blank workbook and pinned runtime assets. Unexpected files and links prevent publishing. modules.scripts/verify.mjs: Runs the full check sequence, records results against a source fingerprint and refreshes the DKG.
modules.src/ui/Calculation.tsx: Hand-calculation view of one row (Ib, k factors, minimum It, Iz, circuit and total VD), size ladder with pick buttons and the From→To feeder chain. Display only; values come from sheet.ts.
modules.src/ui/Report.tsx: Print-only A3 landscape report (schedule with suggested values marked, KPIs, cable quantities, open issues, Prepared/Checked/Approved block). Uses window.print; the browser saves PDF locally.
modules.src/engine/explain.ts: sizeLadder evaluates every size of the row's rating block through evaluateRow with the same current/VD tests as column AB; feederChain follows first-match From→To links. No independent maths.
modules.src/engine/issues.ts: Derives errors (invalid cells, current/VD FAIL), warnings (None passes, Out of range, duplicate To tags, total-VD chain breaks) and info (missing inputs) from calculated rows. Cell references use Excel row numbers.
modules.src/import/guard.ts: Pre-parse guards: XLSX ZIP central-directory size/entry limits (checkZip) and image header dimensions (imageSize/checkImage, 12,000 px side / 60 MP) before any decoder runs; used by load-list, schematic and drum/catalogue imports.
modules.src/import/schematic.ts: Pure, deterministic schematic-to-load-list engine (no AI). DXF parser (TEXT/MTEXT/ATTRIB, binary/size guards, bounded MTEXT clean-up), glyph/word merging on shared baselines, readFacts (breaker A, poles/phase, kW/HP/W/kVA, PF, diversity, voltage incl. 400/230 pairs but not cable insulation ratings, cable type/cores/size/sets, run length, tags, board names, fed-from/feeds-to, spares, title-block words), circuit-schedule table detection (reuses detectColumns/toSheetRows plus cell rescue), single-line-diagram grouping around breaker ratings for column or row layouts with a proximity fallback, board ownership, From→To feeder chain, deduplication across drawings, inferred values with reasons, and limits (100k text items, 20k per page, 4k breakers per page, 200 pages, 2,000 candidates). Traced line work (from images or rendered PDF pages) gives one row per feeder: the busbar label (board tag first, within 7 text heights above or 15 left of its start) is From for drops and To for incomers; labels attach to the nearest feeder by distance from the nearest part of the text, with the far end counting 4 text heights closer and vertical text along the feeder preferred for the load name. Also reads US/MV notation (6-1/C 500 → 1C, 500 kcmil, 2 sets; 3/0 AWG; ft and miles to metres; MW, MVA), ETAP-style tags (TR:4, 3WTR:1, Bus A), transformer ratings into B, and treats a bare C16 as an MCB rating only on pages that mention MCBs or amps.
modules.src/import/schematic-read.ts: Browser reader for schematics: pdf.js text with page rotation and text direction, OCR (sparse-text mode) for pages without a text layer or for images, UTF-8/Windows-1252 DXF decoding, cancel support, 25 MB/page/text-item limits, image header dimension check before decoding, friendly pdf.js and DWG messages. Images and scanned PDF pages go through drawing-ocr (scale up to 2x for small screenshots, 24 MP working budget); vector PDF pages are rendered to trace busbars and feeders under the text layer. Returns the text read for the review.
modules.src/ui/Schematic.tsx: Review dialog for circuits read from a schematic: tick/untick rows, page and source text per row, worked-out values in italics with their reason, notes (spares skipped, unsupported voltages, DC, unticked fed-from feeders), Create load list / Add to current list. Opens even when no circuits are recognised, explaining why and showing the text that was read; a collapsible "Text read from the drawing" panel is always available.
modules.src/import/raster.ts: Pure image helpers for drawings (plain RGBA arrays, linear in pixels): luminance, Otsu threshold, ink mask, line mask that ignores strongly coloured mark-ups, letter stem height measured from vertical run lengths, straight-stroke detection with thickness, box detection (breaker/symbol outlines found before lines are erased) and outline erasing, OCR clean image with long lines erased, quarter-turn rotation and mapping of rotated word boxes, and feeder tracing: busbars are long horizontal strokes with feeders (two if heavier than other long lines, else three; twice-bent cable routes rejected), feeders are followed through bends and across symbol gaps (breakers, fuses, coils) using an endpoint grid. Limits: 8,000 strokes, 60 busbars, 1,500 feeders.
modules.src/import/drawing-ocr.ts: Image pipeline shared by browser and tests: clean image (threshold, long lines and symbol boxes erased), OCR in three orientations (upright, upward, downward text) with tiling for large sheets, noise filter for short words, lone capitals kept only after an adjacent word of similar height, de-duplication of words read twice, then busbar/feeder tracing with text masked. The OCR engine is injected. Also tokenBox, traceLines (vector PDF pages) and scaleGeometry.
modules.src/engine/loads.ts: Equipment-list engine: row and catalogue shapes, catalogue index and fill (Brand + Model + Configuration), per-row kW/kVAr/load factor, panel and plant totals with operating factors and design margin, and the scenario comparison.

modules.src/ui/Catalogue.tsx: Brand catalogue view: editable entries, brand filter and search, workbook import, export, and the datasheet review dialog (text/OCR or local AI, red unverified values, only-rows-to-check filter, page view with a box round each value read, tick to add; blank models and repeated model + configuration refused). modules.src/ui/Scenario.tsx: Search across panels by KKS/description, scenario comparison table and inline-SVG grouped bar charts, plant load by panel.
modules.src/export/equipment-layout.ts: Panel sheet layout: header rows 1-6, at least 32 item rows, the running plant load, operating factors and load basis summary, page setup; formulas with cached results.
modules.src/import/vocabulary.ts: Rating-table field vocabulary as data: words for kW, current, voltage, efficiency, power factor, speed, poles, type/series names, part codes, frame sizes and not-load-data columns in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Russian and Chinese, plus symbols and units matched as printed; fieldsIn scores a heading line (longest phrase first, abbreviations by prefix).
modules.src/import/rating-table.ts: Columns are named by vocabulary.ts in any listed language, checked against their values, and found from P = √3·U·I·η·cosφ when no heading is understood; type/series name = model, row-distinguishing code (product ID, frame) = configuration, title product name for size-only tables. Catalogue rating tables (one row per motor/pump/fan) read by column position from PDF item x/width: columns from overlapping numbers, stacked headings classified bottom-up (kW, hp, In at 400 V, efficiency/power factor at full load; starting current, torque, weight skipped), poles from speed or sub-headings, voltage/Hz/phase from the heading context. Rows are checked against P = √3·U·I·η·cosφ (In/Un flagged when they do not add up); a name column repeated down the table goes into the configuration, and every value keeps its page box for the review's page view.
modules.src/import/webpage.ts: Vendor product web pages pasted from the browser or saved as .html: HTML to text (regex, never rendered), label/value pairs and comparison tables to catalogue proposals, HP to kW, checked with verify. Also reads PDF datasheets laid out as label/value columns (catalogueFromDatasheet): long labels match by their known start only with the field's unit, signal inputs and losses skipped, ligatures and wrapped labels rejoined, brand from label, title or copyright.

calculationReference.electrical: I1 = kW × diversity × 1000 / (V × PF × (sqrt(3) for 3-phase, else 1)); Ib = I1 × sqrt(1 + THD²); Iz = It × parallel × Ca × Cg × Cs × Ci × Ct; circuit VD% = Ib × run_m × mV/A/m / (10 × parallel × V).
calculationReference.suggestedSize: Preserves original workbook row-order/count-failing-candidates formula. Source ratings are ordered contiguous blocks; do not replace it independently of Excel parity.
calculationReference.upstream: Total VD uses the first To matching From. Blank From gives blank total VD. A nonblank unmatched From is a supply boundary with zero upstream VD.
calculationReference.earthFaultLoop: TN-S and TT, SS 638:2018 / IEC 60364 (step08 AP-BG). Earthing system per row (AP, blank = Settings Def_Earthing TN-S). U0 = nominal (V/sqrt3 rounded to 10 V for 3-ph, V for 1-ph). Required disconnection time = SS 638 Table 41.1 by system and U0 for final circuits (In <= 32 A, To feeds no row): TN-S 0.8/0.4/0.2/0.1 s, TT 0.3/0.2/0.07/0.04 s; else TN-S 5 s (411.3.2.3L), TT 1 s (411.3.2.4L). R1+R2 = (r20 phase x m phase + r20 CPC x m CPC) x run / (1000 x parallel). Zs = Ze + R1+R2 (TT Ze typed or from a TT feeding row). Max = larger of the overcurrent limit (TN-S Cmin x U0 / Ia, 411.4.5L; TT 50 / Ia, 411.5.4L) and the RCD limit 50 / IDn (TN-S 411.4.5L, TT 411.5.3L / Table 41.5). Check: TN-S Zs <= max; TT Ra (typed) or Zs <= max. Ia = 5/10/20 x In for MCB B/C/D or typed. If = U0/Zs. CPC: Table 54.2 minimum; PASS by selection when CPC >= minimum, else adiabatic (k2 x S x n)^2 >= If^2 x t. Computed by the app (faultCells) and checked against tests/fixtures/excel-fault-crosscheck.json (165 circuits).
calculationReference.shortCircuit: IEC 60364-4-43:2023 431.5.4 (step08 BH-BO): breaking capacity >= fault level at From (431.5.4.1). I2t = typed let-through or (Ik_from x 1000)^2 x t; min size = sqrt(I2t)/(k x parallel), k from 4-43 Table 2 (115/103 PVC, 143 XLPE); PASS when size >= min, else FAIL, or 'Check let-through' for an MCB row with no let-through (431.5.4.2: below 0.1 s the device let-through applies). Ik_to = Ik_from / sqrt(1 + (m x r20 x run/(1000 x parallel) x Ik_from x 1000 / U0)^2), m 1 (3-ph) or 2 (1-ph). Computed by the app and checked against tests/fixtures/excel-fault-crosscheck.json (165 circuits).

dataContracts.worksheet: Record of input column letters to strings; derived results are recomputed.
dataContracts.physicalDimensions: OD in mm, cable mass in kg/km, minimum bend radius as a multiple of OD.
dataContracts.drumDimensions: Flange/barrel/winding width/clearance in mm; payload/tare/lift in kg; allowance in percent.
dataContracts.migration: Older device autosaves (IndexedDB) are deleted on start, not restored. Earlier circuit/catalogue models are not silently converted.

knownLimits: Electrical calculations reproduce the supplied workbook; a PASS covers its current-capacity and voltage-drop checks, not a complete certified installation design.
Stored fixture provenance says Microsoft Excel recalculated 260 rows on 2026-10-28. Regression tests compare those recorded values; they do not launch Excel on every run.
Imported XLSX formulas use saved results, which can be stale. The UI asks engineers to recalculate/save the source before import.
Duplicate To tags retain the workbook's first-match semantics. Engineers must resolve ambiguous network names; cycles cannot provide a meaningful total VD.
The original workbook's underground grouping table repeats factors beyond six circuits. These are preserved for parity and require engineering validation for the actual arrangement.
No automatic cable diameter, mass or bend-radius inference from cross-section. Dimensions must match the exact product and be confirmed for each selected group.
Single-core run counts omit neutral and earth. Add separately when their product/size differs or plan explicit typed runs when extra conductors are required.
Supplier PDF/OCR extraction handles explicitly labelled units, not arbitrary unlabeled tabulations. Use reviewed CSV/XLSX or manual adaptor inputs when extraction is incomplete.
No cable-catalogue/IEC electrical workflow, authentication, multi-user revisions, purchase orders, cloud backend or published site is active in this version.
Browser session restore can retain work. Save a JSON backup for deliberate long-term storage.
Undo history is lost on reload. Use JSON backups for checkpoints.
Print/PDF relies on the browser print dialog; choose A3 landscape and enable background graphics for PASS/FAIL shading.
Duplicated or restored tabs can hold separate copies. Clear this tab’s data removes its autosave and undo history. Exported files are ordinary files on the device.
A real HTTPS deployment still needs response-header, artifact, injected-script and host-log review. See docs/security-review.md.
The drum turntable animates with requestAnimationFrame, so browsers pause it in hidden tabs or panes.

Schematic recognition is rule-based. It reads text, not line work: connections are inferred from where annotations sit (around each breaker rating, in schedule tables or in CAD block attributes). Unusual layouts can group text wrongly, so the review step is mandatory reading. Tags are taken as written; differently spelt board names (MSB1 vs MSB-1) are not linked.

Image reading (screenshots, scans, PDFs without a text layer) uses on-device OCR in three orientations plus line tracing of busbars and feeders. It handles orthogonal single-line diagrams; diagonal lines, dense overlapping labels, red-line mark-ups over text and very small text (under about 10 px) read poorly. Numbers from OCR must be checked in the review.

DWG is not readable; export ASCII DXF or PDF. Binary DXF and block-definition text other than attributes are not read. AWG/kcmil sizes, DC systems and voltages outside the workbook list are kept but cannot be sized by the workbook.

The workbook ratings cover LV cables (230–690 V). Medium/high-voltage drawings (e.g. 13.8 kV, 138 kV) are read and listed with their drawing voltage, but rows show as invalid on the sheet until MV rating tables are supplied.

Earth fault loop, RCD, CPC and short-circuit columns AP-BO cover TN-S and TT only (SS 638:2018, IEC 60364). Ze and fault level default to blank (not assumed); a TT row needs Ze typed or a TT feeding row. Not modelled: TN-C, TN-C-S and IT systems, cable reactance (Zs reads low above about 35 mm2), the IEC 60909 voltage factor c and minimum fault currents, RCD discrimination, the TN-S times allowed for a bonded TT installation on an overcurrent device, electrode stability above 200 ohms, Annex A.3 exemptions, fuse Zs tables (type Ia). A separate copper CPC is taken as PVC-insulated and not bunched; armour and tape need catalogue area and resistance.

Load list: the export's intermittent reactive operating-factor formula intentionally follows the supplied template, which can differ from the app's total-load calculation. The panel sheet matches the designed "Panel 1" cell for cell (except the KKS heading); it has not been opened in Excel here, so the print preview is unchecked. Text placeholders in consumed load, efficiency or power factor are left out of the export. Scenario inputs are not saved; the In vs Ib check is not run on send; one header block per sheet is read on import; the equipment grid has no arrow-key navigation.

Use the graph to locate relevant files; read those files before editing. Update docs/project-knowledge.json when semantics change, run checks, refresh the DKG. Run tests/hardening.test.ts; any new file or text input needs size limits and a hostile-input test.
